newsitem.title: USA: Swiss banks agree to unveil Holocaust accounts-NYC.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks agree to unveil Holocaust accounts-NYC.

text.p: The New York City Comptroller, who last week met with major Swiss banks about how Holocaust victims were treated, said Wednesday he had a tentative agreement for them to publish data about dormant accounts.
Alan Hevesi, in a prepared statement, said that further details would be provided at a news conference later this morning.
The release added: "He will also correct a misunderstanding about the purpose of the 7.0 billion Swiss franc fund."
The three Swiss banks with whom the city comptroller met were: CS Group, Union Bank of Switzerland and Swiss Bank Corp.
Hevesi is a trustee and investment advisor for the city's $70 billion pension fund, which owned stock in the three banks as of Dec 31, 1996.
Hevesi also spoke with Swiss government officials and Swiss Jewish leaders while he was in the country.

The New York City Council, which considered whether to require the city's pensions to divest themselves of Swiss banks' stocks, put the proposal on hold after the Swiss government in February created a fund for Holocaust victims.

The fund was set up to defuse the country's worst foreign policy crisis since World War II, which was sparked by allegations that Swiss banks hoarded unclaimed wealth of Holocaust victims and that neutral Switzerland cynically profited from the war.
